page: Amazon Web Services r6a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at 3.6 GHz with 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 8 MB L3 cache per slice. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while advanced matrix extensions and AVX-512 variants are not available on this platform.

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It lacks local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is absent, with 0 GPUs assigned to this instance configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a stress-ng score in the top 25% and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1666.0. However, multi-core throughput is constrained by the 4-vCPU topology, placing multi-threaded benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core in the bottom 25%. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 38.45 GB/sec for read operations and 22.57 GB/sec for writes. Workloads involving Redis set operations and static web serving register in the bottom quartile.

From a cost efficiency and architectural standpoint, the r6a.xlarge delivers substantial memory density per core via AMD hardware, avoiding the overhead of high CPU allocations when only large memory capacity is required. It is well aligned with memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive parallel compute, such as distributed in-memory caching tiers, mid-sized relational database instances, ETL data staging, and application background jobs.
